messages.subject: Occupancy modelling for migratory birds
parts:
Hi all, I have a question regarding the applicability of occupancy models. I hope someone can clarify this concept for me. 

 Is it applicable to non-breeding migratory birds in their wintering habitats given the fact that, albeit it's a part of their life cycle, the occupancy is transient in nature? 

Any insight will be much appreciated. Thank you all!

Kind regards,
Jose

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Occupancy modelling for migratory birds
parts:
Dear Jose,

yes, absolutely. The main thing is that you must be able to define some period during which the so-called closure assumption is met to a good degree. That means, that no site makes a state transition during this period from presence -> absence or vice versa. If you are studying insects, then this period may be as short as a couple of days. For wintering birds I assume we're talking about a couple of months.

Best regards  --- Marc
